item: WT vs mutant root batch confound
question: WT root libraries (sample_fastq RS1RM1SS01-08, curated under TorresRodriguez2021) form a separate library/sequencing batch from all 16 mutant root libraries (SG1TM1001-1016). Root genotype contrasts (het/hom vs WT) are therefore confounded with batch. N contrasts within het or hom are not affected. How to handle?
proposed_answer: Use N contrasts within each mutant genotype only; do not build root WT-vs-mutant contrasts (or flag them as batch-confounded). Leaf libraries of all genotypes share lanes, so leaf genotype contrasts are not batch-confounded by genotype.
evidence: BioSample sample_fastq: WT roots RS1RM1SS0x, het/hom roots SG1TM10xx; WT and mutant leaves share DRRS001/DRRS002; all roots NextSeq 550

question: Leaf lane batch DRRS001 holds every full-P leaf library and DRRS002 every low-P leaf library (all genotypes). N contrasts within P level are unaffected; P effects in leaf are confounded with lane.
proposed_answer: Build N contrasts within tissue x P level x genotype only.
evidence: BioSample sample_fastq vs treatment

question: Heterozygous (pho1;2a'-m1.1/+) plants are curated as a separate mutant genotype with their own N contrasts. Keep het as an N-contrast genotype, or drop it and keep only homozygotes?
proposed_answer: Keep both het and hom as separate genotypes (paper reports misregulation in het too); contrasts can choose.
evidence: BioSample genotype W22/pho1;2a'-m1.1 (het) vs pho1;2a'-m1.1/pho1;2a'-m1.1 (hom); paper Fig. S4 (heterozygous effects)

question: This sheet has only the 32 het/hom runs; the 16 WT runs of the same experiment are under TorresRodriguez2021. Any genotype contrast needs them from there.
proposed_answer: Leave WT under TorresRodriguez2021 (owner); reference them from contrasts.tsv when needed.
evidence: runs.tsv study_id/also_used_by; Methods: WT siblings analysed previously in Torres-Rodriguez et al. 2021

question: Two single-plant replicates per genotype x tissue x treatment.
proposed_answer: Keep; weights will reflect it.
evidence: Methods: two biological replicates

question: All 6 Low-N libraries were sequenced as PE36 in one GA II run (files s_1-s_6) and all 6 High-N libraries as PE40 in another (files 2_s_1-2_s_6), so N level is fully confounded with sequencing run and read length.
proposed_answer: Keep include = TRUE; trim all reads to 36 nt before quantification and flag the contrast as batch-confounded.
evidence: ENA run_alias (submitted file names) and runs.tsv read_length; PMC3912931 Methods (2 x 36 or 2 x 40 bp).

question: One pooled library (2-3 plants) per genotype x N x tissue; no biological replicates.
proposed_answer: Keep; mark contrasts as unreplicated.
evidence: PMC3912931 Methods; accessions_resolved.tsv.

question: SRG150 is the hybrid of SRG100 and SRG200; the female parent is not stated.
proposed_answer: genotype SRG150, genotype_class hybrid, background SRG150; cross direction NR.
evidence: PMC3912931 Methods (Plant materials and growth condition).

question: age_days 30 is computed as 2 d germination in Turface + 4 weeks in hydroponics (harvest four weeks after transplanting).
proposed_answer: Accept 30 d.
evidence: PMC3912931 Methods.

question: Neither the paper nor GEO gives the N concentration of the normal-N (NN) and recovery solutions, and they disagree on the base solution (paper: Magnavaca solution; GEO: full-strength Hoagland). N_amount set to NR. Look up?
proposed_answer: Keep NR (N_form nitrate); if needed, ask the authors or adopt the Magnavaca et al. 1987 recipe with a note.
evidence: Paper Methods (PMC12714369): Magnavaca nutrient solution, Ca(NO3)2 replaced by CaCl2 for LN; GEO GSE312408 growth protocol: Hoagland, Ca(NO3)2 and Mg(NO3)2 replaced by CaCl2 and MgSO4

question: LN removes all nitrate salts; neither source says whether any ammonium remained. Coded LN as N_form none, N_amount 0. Accept?
proposed_answer: Accept (nitrate-free LN treated as no-N); revisit if the recipe shows an ammonium salt.
evidence: Paper: 'all nitrate salts were removed from the medium'; GEO: nitrate-limiting solution

question: Aliases T0/T30min/T3h/T1d/T1d30min/T2d decoded as 0, 0.5, 3, 24 h LN and 24.5, 48 h (0.5 and 24 h after nitrate re-supply). Per the project rule, time_h uses one experiment clock (h since nitrate removal): recovery samples are 24.5 and 48 h with phase resupply (re-supply happened at 24 h, so they are 0.5 and 24 h after re-supply). Accept?
proposed_answer: Accept; hours since re-supply (0.5, 24) are stated in curation_note.
evidence: GEO GSE312408 sample titles (e.g. 'T24.5h Leaves 1-NR', 'T48h Root 2-NR') and characteristics time: 0h ... 48h, matched by BioSample; GEO treatment protocol says '24h + 30 min and 24h + 48 h' (the latter conflicts with the 48 h total in titles and paper; taken as 24 h recovery)

question: Paper and GEO disagree on several protocol details: transfer to hydroponics after 3 d (paper) vs 7 DAG (GEO); 10-15 plants pooled (paper) vs 5 (GEO); Epicentre ScriptSeq + HiSeq 2500 (paper) vs NEBNext + NextSeq 2000 (GEO protocol) while SRA/GEO instrument is HiSeq 4000 PE101. Which to record?
proposed_answer: Use the paper for design (pool of 10-15 plants, noted in curation_note with pooled_plants left empty; 15 DAG at treatment) and note SRA instrument; no effect on contrasts since all 36 libraries share one submission.
evidence: PMC12714369 Methods; GSE312408 sample protocols; runs.tsv instrument

question: The paper's RNA-seq methods list only 0.5-48 h, but 6 T0 (NN, 0 h) libraries are deposited. Use T0 as the NN reference for all LN and recovery contrasts?
proposed_answer: Yes: T0 is the only normal-N sample; contrasts LN(t) vs T0 and recovery vs T1d (24 h LN).
evidence: GEO GSM9345258-60 (leaves) and GSM9345276-78 (roots): treatment normal nitrogen, time 0h

question: The GEO labels ’Nitrogen’ and ’Urea + Nitrogen’ (and the study brief’s ’nitrate, urea + nitrate’) suggest nitrate. What N form was actually supplied?
proposed_answer: Ammonium: ’Nitrogen’ = 100A (1 mM (NH4)2SO4) -> N_form ammonium; ’Urea + Nitrogen’ = 50U:50A -> N_form mixed (urea + ammonium). No nitrate treatment; the accessions_resolved note should be corrected.
evidence: PMC8597056 Methods 2.1 (100U, 50U:50A, 100A, -N; ’no detectable nitrate was present in all nutrient solutions’); GEO overall design ’100% Urea, 50% Urea and 50% N, and 100% N’.

question: Seedlings germinated on CaSO4 and were moved to hydroponics at day 3. The solution for days 3-5 isn’t specified; at day 5 they went into N-free solution with or without N for 24 h.
proposed_answer: Settled by the project phase rule: N treatments = resupply, -N = starvation (time-matched control), time_h 24.
evidence: PMC8597056 Methods 2.1; RNA-seq on roots after 1 d of treatment.

question: Total N of the ’complete Hoagland’ control is not given; only that 0N replaces 1 mM KNO3 with equimolar KCl. Is 1 mM nitrate the full CT N supply?
proposed_answer: Use N_amount 1 mM nitrate for CT (the ’0N’ label implies KNO3 is the only N source); confirm from Quaggiotti et al. 2024 / authors.
evidence: PMC13348872 Methods 2.1 and GEO treatment protocol: ’1 mM KNO3 was replaced by equimolar KCl’; treatment named 0N.

question: WS plants got the complete solution only at transplanting and no further irrigation, so their cumulative N supply is lower than CT and confounded with drought. How should they be ranked?
proposed_answer: Keep N fields equal to CT (rank 2) and other_factor water = water stress; use WS only for water-stress or genotype contrasts, never in N contrasts.
evidence: PMC13348872 Methods 2.1; GEO treatment protocol.

question: Plants were 28 d after transplanting (older than 21 d) but small (4th leaf only just present in CT; absent in WS). Seedling or vegetative?
proposed_answer: seedling (about V3-V4; paper calls them seedlings).
evidence: PMC13348872 Results 3.2 (fourth leaf not yet developed in WS after 28 d); figure legends say ’seedlings’.

question: Paper and GEO say zmccd8::Ds is in the B73 background. Ds insertion lines usually come from the W22 Ac/Ds collection; was it backcrossed into B73?
proposed_answer: Keep background B73 as stated; low priority check of the allele source (Guan et al. 2012).
evidence: PMC13348872 Methods 2.1 (’in the same genetic background’); GEO growth protocol (’in the B73 genetic background’).

question: Four plants pooled per biological replicate is stated in the RNA-extraction section that covers qRT-PCR. Does it also apply to the RNA-seq root libraries?
proposed_answer: Assume 4 (same RNA extracts), as recorded.
evidence: PMC13348872 Methods 2.3; GEO overall design says 3 biological replicates per genotype x treatment, without a pool size.

question: The paper has zmnrt1.1b-1 and zmnrt1.1b-2 and two zmnlp3.1 alleles, but doesn’t say which allele was sequenced.
proposed_answer: Use ’zmnrt1.1b’ and ’zmnlp3.1’ without an allele suffix; ask the authors only if allele-level detail matters.
evidence: PMC10826987 Results (zmnrt1.1b-1/-2 phenotypes; ’two loss-of-function mutants of ZmNLP3.1’); Methods (CAU stocks CAUC0713/CAUC0714/CAUC1783).

question: GEO calls both mutants ’knockdown’, but the paper describes CRISPR/Cas9 loss-of-function lines.
proposed_answer: genotype_class = mutant (CRISPR knockouts), background ND101.
evidence: PMC10826987 Results and Methods (CRISPR/Cas9 in ND101).

question: WT is not named for the RNA-seq; the mutants are in ND101.
proposed_answer: WT = ND101 (other inbred).
evidence: PMC10826987 Methods: ’loss-of-function mutants in the background of ND101’.

question: GEO titles use replicate numbers with gaps (KCl_WT_1-3, KNO3_WT_1/3/4, KCl_1_1b_2-4, KNO3_1_1b_2/4/5, KCl_3_1_1/3/4, KNO3_3_1_2-4), so more replicates were probably grown or sequenced and three deposited per group.
proposed_answer: Renumber 1-3 within each group (original number kept in curation_note); don’t pair KCl and KNO3 replicates by number.
evidence: GEO GSE227472 sample titles; series design ’18 samples with 3 biological replicats’.

question: The KCl mock samples are N-starved seedlings sampled 2 h after mock treatment. Should they be phase resupply at time_h 2?
proposed_answer: Settled by the project phase rule: KNO3 = resupply, KCl = starvation (N_amount 0), both time_h 2. age_days 20 = 6 d + 10 d + 4 d (Methods).
evidence: PMC10826987 Methods ’Growth conditions’.

question: The paper analysed 8 libraries (2 plot replicates per genotype x N), but SRA has 4 runs. Each run spot count equals the sum of the two replicate trimmed-read counts in Table 1 (e.g. NN Zheng58 23,736,829 vs 11,711,873 + 12,024,837 = 23,736,710), so each run is two biological replicates concatenated.
proposed_answer: Treat each run as one sample (n = 1 per group, pooled_plants 8). Splitting would need replicate tags in the FASTQ read names (not checked: no sequence download) or the authors.
evidence: PMC4569664 Table 1 and Methods; runs.tsv n_spots; accessions_resolved.tsv (4 runs, unreplicated).

question: The NN rate is given as '450 kg/ha urea'. Recorded as N_amount 450, N_unit 'kg urea/ha'. If this is urea mass, it is about 207 kg N/ha (46% N).
proposed_answer: Convert to 207 kg N/ha (urea) for pooling, keeping the reported value in the note.
evidence: PMC4569664 Methods (Plant materials).

question: LN plots were in locations not fertilized for the preceding 2 years, so NN and LN were grown in different fields; field effects are confounded with N.
proposed_answer: Accept (typical for field N trials); note in the contrast.
evidence: PMC4569664 Methods (Plant materials).

question: The tissue is the 'leaf above the primary ear' (BioSample and paper), not the ear leaf itself.
proposed_answer: Keep tissue_detail 'leaf above the primary ear'.
evidence: PMC4569664 Methods; BioSample tissue attribute.

question: GEO says 91 samples from 16 genotypes, but 19 genotype labels are deposited (10 inbreds incl. B73, 9 B73 hybrids). Which 16 were used in the paper's models is not stated. Keep all 19?
proposed_answer: Keep all; FR1064 (no highN) cannot enter a within-genotype N contrast; decide at contrasts.tsv.
evidence: GSE152249 overall design; per-genotype highN/lowN counts: B73 3/3; B73xIHP1 3/1; B73xILP1 3/2; B73xLH82 3/2; B73xMo17 3/1; B73xMo18W 3/2; B73xOh7B 3/2; B73xPH207 3/3; B73xPHG47 3/2; B73xPHG84 2/2; FR1064 0/1; IHP1 3/3; ILP1 2/2; IRHP1 1/1; LH82 3/3; Mo17 2/3; PH207 3/4; PHG84 3/3; W22 3/2

question: Only some genotype x N groups have 3 replicates; unbalanced genotypes: B73xIHP1, B73xILP1, B73xLH82, B73xMo17, B73xMo18W, B73xOh7B, B73xPHG47, B73xPHG84, FR1064, ILP1, IRHP1, Mo17, PH207, W22. Several arms have a single library (e.g. B73xIHP1 lowN, B73xMo17 lowN, IRHP1 both). Fit per-genotype contrasts only where both arms have >= 2 reps, else pool via genotype + N model?
proposed_answer: Per-genotype log2FC where each arm has >= 2 libraries; otherwise include only in a pooled ~ genotype + N model.
evidence: GEO titles (replicate numbers have gaps, e.g. Rep1 and Rep3 only)

question: PH207 lowN has Rep3 (GSM4610060) and Rep3-2 (GSM4610059), both separate libraries labelled replicate 3. Technical duplicate or a 4th plant?
proposed_answer: Treat as a technical duplicate of Rep3: merge counts with Rep3 or drop Rep3-2 at QC (both rows kept here with replicate 3).
evidence: GEO titles PH207_lowN_Rep3 / PH207_lowN_Rep3-2; SRR11993798 / SRR11993797

question: RNA samples were taken in 2014 (paper Fig. 3c legend) at R1; N was granular ammonium sulfate (200 kg N/ha) vs none, coded N_form ammonium. Accept?
proposed_answer: Accept.
evidence: PMC8463701 Methods (maize) and Fig. 3c legend: 'The total NUtE variance of 2014, the year when the RNA samples were harvested'

question: Split-plot design pairs N-replete and N-depleted rows within main plots, so replicate numbers may mark field blocks shared by highN and lowN. Not confirmed. Model block?
proposed_answer: Do not model block unless the authors confirm; note as possible pairing.
evidence: Paper Methods: individuals in each main plot were paired in adjacent rows of N-replete or N-depleted condition

question: The paper gives no accession; PRJNA556506 aliases match its design exactly (B73, SN/NN, 9 time points). Accept as Du2020 data?
proposed_answer: Accept (resolved by repository match).
evidence: ENA sample aliases B73_HN_0..8 / B73_LN_0..8; JAAS submitter; registered 2019-07

question: One pooled sample per time point and treatment: treat as unreplicated in DESeq2 (or model time as continuous)?
proposed_answer: Mark contrasts replicated = FALSE; consider a time-course model (e.g. spline over time x treatment) at M4.
evidence: Paper Methods: one biological replicate (pool of 3 plants) per time point

question: Normal-N (NN) and low-N (LN) concentrations and N form are not available: paper is not in PMC, ScienceDirect blocks scripted access and the JIA page shows only the abstract. Recorded N_form/N_amount/N_unit = NR; ranks LN=1, NN=2.
proposed_answer: Get the PDF manually (open access, CC BY-NC-ND) and fill N_amount/N_form from Methods; keep the study with NR meanwhile (ranks are enough for LN vs NN contrasts).
evidence: Crossref 10.1016/S2095-3119(20)63220-8; chinaagrisci.com abstract page (hydroponic, 5 d low-N); Elsevier API 400, ScienceDirect 403

question: Abstract: phenotypes after 5 d of low-N stress in hydroponics; all BioSamples say age '5 Days'. Not clear whether plants were transferred from NN to LN for 5 d (short-term) or grown on LN from the start. Recorded phase = steady, time_h empty.
proposed_answer: Keep steady; if Methods show a transfer, set phase starvation (if LN is N-free) and time_h = 120.
evidence: chinaagrisci.com abstract (Chinese and English); BioSample age attribute

question: BioSample 'ecotype' says 'low phosphate root repeat1' / 'normal phosphate ...' while titles and isolate say low/normal nitrogen. Mapping follows sample titles (LN/NN).
proposed_answer: Treat as submitter typo; no action.
evidence: runs.tsv biosample_attributes for SAMN14236945-SAMN14236960

question: PRJNA609156 is linked to the paper by BioProject title/description match (16 libraries of leaves and roots of Qi319 and Ye478), not by a data statement read in the paper. BioSample provider Wen-Xue Li is the senior author. Accept?
proposed_answer: Accept (title, design, institution and senior author all match).
evidence: accessions_resolved.tsv Du2021 row; BioSample biomaterial_provider Wen-Xue Li; 16 runs = 2 genotypes x 2 tissues x 2 N x 2 reps

question: Catalogue lists leaf; BioSamples say Shoot and the Chinese abstract says aerial part. Curated as Shoot.
proposed_answer: Keep Shoot.
evidence: BioSample tissue Shoot; abstract

question: Paper says 'seedlings (WT+N or WT-N, zmnlp5+N or zmnlp5-N) were collected' and BioSample tissue is 'seedling'; the nitrate qPCR experiments used roots. Curated as whole seedling. Confirm it was not roots only.
proposed_answer: Keep Whole seedling (both paper and BioSample say seedling).
evidence: Methods (Plant materials and growth conditions; Transcriptome analysis); BioSample tissue attribute

question: -N samples got 15 mM KCl for 30 min after 14 d N deprivation. Coded N_form none, N_amount 0, phase starvation, time_h 0.5 (same convention as Du2020/Wu2024 KCl controls); +N coded resupply, 15 mM nitrate, time_h 0.5.
proposed_answer: Keep; contrast = +N vs -N within genotype at 30 min.
evidence: Methods: supplied with 15 mM KNO3 or 15 mM KCl, collected after 30 min

question: The paper’s third zone (maturation zone, 50-150 mm from tip; HMZ/LMZ x 2) isn’t in this study’s runs.
proposed_answer: Borrow Mu2017_HN_R1, Mu2017_HN_R2, Mu2017_LN_R1 and Mu2017_LN_R2 (SRR6335599-610, GSE107562) for the Guo2022 MZ contrast; they are curated under Mu2017 with other_factor_level ’maturation zone’. Count them once when pooling.
evidence: PMC9230787 Methods 3.2 and data statement (GSE107562 and GSE111425); runs.tsv also_used_by = Guo2022 on the Mu2017 runs.

question: GSE111425’s title and summary describe a gibberellin / leaf-growth paper by the same group, not Guo2022, and GSE99638 is a re-upload of the elongation-zone libraries.
proposed_answer: Use GSE111425 runs here (Guo2022 cites them); don’t use GSE99638. If the GA paper is ever catalogued, these libraries must not be counted twice.
evidence: GEO GSE111425 title; accessions_resolved.tsv (GSE99638 duplicate note).

question: Are the DZ/EZ (GSE111425) and MZ (GSE107562) libraries from one sequencing batch?
proposed_answer: Likely yes: library IDs I345-I356 run contiguously and all are lane L4 (e.g. H1_L4_I350 here, H7_L4_I356 in Mu2017), so no zone-batch confounding is expected.
evidence: GEO sample titles/descriptions in GSE111425 and GSE107562.

question: Sampling date or plant age isn’t stated (LN from V3; leaf 6 sampled while expanding).
proposed_answer: Leave age_days empty.
evidence: PMC9230787 Methods 3.1-3.2.

question: The RNA-seq section does not name the line and BioSample cultivar is empty. Use B73?
proposed_answer: B73 (all N-treatment physiology in the paper uses B73; transgenic lines are CZ01 background and were not sequenced). Could be confirmed from reads if needed.
evidence: PMC10363476 Results: 'we grew inbred line B73 under NS, NL or ND'; RNA-seq paragraph follows the B73 Casparian strip experiments; reads mapped to B73 RefGen_v4.

question: Both groups were switched from 4 mM nitrate 3 d before sampling (NL up to 8 mM, ND down to 0.04 mM; the 4 mM NS control was not sequenced). Under the project phase rule this is coded ND = starvation, NL = resupply, time_h 72. Acceptable, or treat this 3-d level treatment as steady?
proposed_answer: Keep starvation/resupply with time_h 72 (N supply changed at time 0 for both groups); the only contrast is ND vs NL at the same time point.
evidence: PMC10363476 Methods: NS/NL/ND imposed from day 5 of hydroponics; RNA-seq after 3 d of NL or ND.

question: The rtcs mutant came from the Maize Genetics Cooperation Stock Center; its genetic background is not reported, while the wild type is B73. Genotype contrasts are confounded with background; N contrasts within genotype are not affected.
proposed_answer: background = NR for rtcs; use within-genotype N contrasts (low-N vs normal-N at each time point) and treat rtcs as a mutant line of unknown background.
evidence: PMC4798287 Methods (Plant materials preparation); BioSample cultivar rtcs.

question: Seedlings were germinated without stated nutrient supply and moved at the two-leaf stage (endosperm removed) to 4 mM or 0.04 mM NO3-, then sampled 12-96 h later. Low-N is coded starvation and normal-N steady, both with time_h 12/24/48/96 so contrasts can be time-matched. OK?
proposed_answer: Yes; build one low-N vs normal-N contrast per genotype and time point (8 contrasts, 2 reps each).
evidence: PMC4798287 Methods; BioSample treatment attribute (e.g. Low-N 12h).

question: Codes I-IV map to 12, 24, 48 and 96 h.
proposed_answer: Confirmed: paper labels samples RNI-IV, RLI-IV, WNI-IV, WLI-IV successively for 12, 24, 48 and 96 h, and BioSample treatment strings agree for all 16 BioSamples.
evidence: PMC4798287 Methods (RNA-Seq library construction); runs.tsv biosample_attributes.

question: Each BioSample has two SRX/runs (library names X_1 and X_2). Are these biological replicates?
proposed_answer: Yes: paper says two independent replicates per sample (3 seedlings each); S4 Table lists X_1 and X_2 with total reads = 2 x run spots. S4 Table omits WNIV_1 (SRR3138231) but the paper states 32 samples; keep it.
evidence: PMC4798287 Methods and S4 Table (pone.0151697.s010); ENA library_name.

question: MTS120mS3-N (SRR31123507) has 24,440 reads (study median 6,925,974). Set include = FALSE. Agree?
proposed_answer: Exclude; shoot +N at 120 min keeps 2 replicates.
evidence: runs.tsv n_spots

question: Root -N 120 min has 4 libraries (MTS120mR1-4-noN) while the design states 3 per time point per treatment. Keep the 4th?
proposed_answer: Keep as replicate 4 (separate GSM8594908 / BioSample); nothing suggests a duplicate.
evidence: GEO GSE280345; paper Methods: three biological replicates per time point per treatment

question: Time 0 has one set of 3 libraries per tissue (treatment noN), shared by +N and -N series. Coded phase starvation, time_h 0, N 0. Use as the common baseline for both arms?
proposed_answer: Yes; per-time-point +N vs -N contrasts are the primary comparison, T0 is the shared baseline.
evidence: GEO treatment 'noN' for MTS0mS1-3 and MTS0mR1-3-noN; paper: harvested at 0, 5, ... 120 min

question: All 115 libraries are Lexogen QuantSeq 3' mRNA-seq with UMIs (one read per transcript 3' end); needs a 3'-aware quantification (UMI dedup, no length normalisation). Flag for processing?
proposed_answer: Process with UMI-tools dedup + gene-level counts; treat effect sizes as comparable to full-length RNA-seq log2FC.
evidence: Paper Methods; GEO data processing

question: Only one HN control (DN0, time 0) was sequenced; no time-matched HN samples exist for DN3-DN96 or RN3-RN24. How should starvation and resupply contrasts be formed?
proposed_answer: Starvation: DNt vs DN0 (rank 1 vs 2, same tissue). Resupply: RNt vs DN96 (N added back) and optionally RNt vs DN0. Flag that time/plant age and diurnal effects are confounded with N in all contrasts.
evidence: PMC10454388 Methods 4.9: RNA-seq samples at 0, 3, 12, 24, 96 h after deprivation and 3, 12, 24 h after resupply; 48 libraries = 8 time points x 2 tissues x 3 reps (titles X-0, X-DNt, X-RNt).

question: Resupply samples (RN3/12/24) carry time_h = hours since resupply (the second N change, at 96 h of deprivation), while DN samples carry hours since deprivation onset. OK for time-matching?
proposed_answer: Yes: RNt pairs with DN96 (time_h 96 of the starvation phase) as its starved reference; the time-zero HN sample DN0 is phase steady, time_h 0.
evidence: PMC10454388 Methods 4.8-4.9; titles X-RN3/12/24.

question: The Crop Journal paper (doi 10.1016/j.cj.2022.02.004) could not be read; design taken from GEO GSE183171 only (B73, 4 mM Ca(NO3)2 vs 4 mM CaCl2, 2 cm root tips, 4 d). Accept GEO as the source?
proposed_answer: Accept; check the paper PDF by hand if available.
evidence: GEO GSM5856951-54 treatment protocol and characteristics

question: Only 2 bulk replicates per condition. Keep for v1 (SE will be wide)?
proposed_answer: Keep; flag low replication in contrasts.tsv.
evidence: GEO titles replicate 1-2

question: GEO characteristics say '2cm root tips'; the (10x) extract protocol says primary roots were sampled. Coded primary root tip (PO:0020127). Accept?
proposed_answer: Accept (seedlings are 4 d old; primary root dominates).
evidence: GSE183171 sample records

question: The paper describes 12 RNA-seq samples (2 hybrids x 2 N x 3), but SRP341978 has 24 runs: aliases XYC1-3/XYT1-3/HNC1-3/HNT1-3 and XYCa-c/XYTa-c/HNCa-c/HNTa-c. What distinguishes the two sets, and which set is the paper's grain-filling (R3) data?
proposed_answer: Unresolved; do not pool the sets as 6 replicates. Most likely two stages: the same group's companion paper (Wang et al. 2022 Genes 13:670, PMC9030517) sampled uppermost fully expanded leaves of the same hybrids under N0/N240 at V12, and both papers cite the same PRIDE dataset PXD028027 (3 TMT10 plexes = 30 channels, room for 24 samples). Ask the authors (Duan H., Hebei Agricultural University), or infer later from data (clustering by set; senescence/grain-filling markers). Until then stage = NR and other_factor = SRA sample set.
evidence: runs.tsv aliases; BioSample collection_date 2018-08-12 for all 24; PMC10603844 Methods 2.2 (12 samples); PMC9030517 Methods 2.3 (V12, uppermost fully expanded leaf, 12 proteomic samples); PRIDE PXD028027 file list (bjhb1-3 x 10 raw files).

question: RNA-seq Methods say 'uppermost fully expanded leaves'; Methods 2.1 says leaf tissue (~10 cm from the middle of the ear leaf) at R3 for proteomics. Which leaf was sequenced?
proposed_answer: Leaf either way (tissue_group unaffected); tissue_detail records both statements. Resolve together with the set question.
evidence: PMC10603844 Methods 2.1 and 2.2.

question: Was the 5 mM KNO3 of the high-N treatment added on top of complete Hoagland N (2 mM Ca(NO3)2 + 1.25 mM NH4NO3) or did it replace it?
proposed_answer: Most likely added (replacement would give 5 mM N, below the 6.5 mM N control, contradicting the high-N label): HN = 11.5 mM N, mixed (10.25 mM NO3- + 1.25 mM NH4+). Left N_amount and N_form NR until confirmed; rank 2 kept.
evidence: PMC12430503 Methods 4.6: 'transferred to Hoagland nutrient solution ... 5 mM KNO3 was used for high-nitrogen treatment'; complete Hoagland composition listed separately. Micronutrient units in that list (e.g. 10 mM H3BO3, 0.5 mM (NH4)6Mo7O24) look like uM typos.

question: Germination duration before the three-leaf stage is not given, so age_days is empty. OK?
proposed_answer: Leave empty; stage recorded as three-leaf stage + 14 d.
evidence: PMC12430503 Methods 4.6.

question: Split-root design: roots coded by the N in their own compartment (Sp.NO3 = C.NO3 = 4 mM N as nitrate; Sp.Cl = C.Cl = 0), shoots by whole-plant supply (C.Cl rank 1 < Split rank 2 < C.NO3 rank 3); the systemic signal goes in other_factor. Primary N contrasts: C.NO3 vs C.Cl (root, shoot) and Sp.NO3 vs Sp.Cl (paired halves). Accept?
proposed_answer: Accept; treat Sp.NO3 vs C.NO3 and Sp.Cl vs C.Cl (the paper's contrasts) as systemic-signal contrasts, not N-level contrasts.
evidence: PMC13085526 Methods (maize split-root) and Results (661 DEGs Sp.NO3 vs C.NO3; 10,248 Sp.Cl vs C.Cl)

question: Sp.NO3 rep k, Sp.Cl rep k and split shoot rep k probably come from the same 6 plants, but the paper does not say so. Model as paired?
proposed_answer: Assume paired by replicate number for Sp.NO3 vs Sp.Cl only if the authors confirm; otherwise unpaired.
evidence: Paper: split root sample = 6 roots from 6 plants; split shoot sample = 6 seedlings

question: BioSample dev_stage says 4 weeks; Methods add up to ~24 d (4 + 7 + 9 + 2 + 2). age_days set to 24, stage_class seedling (paper calls them seedlings). Accept?
proposed_answer: Accept.
evidence: PMC13085526 Methods; BioSample attribute dev_stage

question: Only one library per N level (2 runs). No within-study variance estimate is possible.
proposed_answer: Keep include = TRUE; flag the contrast as unreplicated (SE not estimable from this study alone).
evidence: accessions_resolved.tsv (2 runs); PMC4865003 Results (two datasets, ~15 Gb SN and ~13 Gb LN); qPCR used 3 independent replicates.

question: BioSample dev_stage is V7 for SN but V8 for LN; the paper says leaves were sampled at V7 for both.
proposed_answer: Use V7 (paper).
evidence: runs.tsv biosample_attributes for SAMN03782434/5; PMC4865003 Methods.

question: Libraries are rRNA-depleted total RNA (RiboMinus), unlike the polyA libraries of most studies; gene-level fold changes should still be comparable but intronic/ncRNA reads are higher.
proposed_answer: Keep; record library type in the contrast or study notes.
evidence: PMC4865003 Methods (RNA extraction, rRNA depletion and total RNA-seq).

question: The 12 libraries are lncRNA-seq (Novogene). The paper does not say whether they are rRNA-depleted and strand-specific (Novogene lncRNA standard) or poly(A). Matters for pooling with poly(A) mRNA-seq studies (intronic/non-polyA signal, gene-level counts).
proposed_answer: Treat as rRNA-depleted total RNA-seq (likely) and mark library type NR; check strandedness from reads during processing.
evidence: Methods: libraries of lncRNAs sequenced on HiSeq 2500 by Novogene; no kit or depletion method named

question: RNA-seq samples are described as '14-day-old seedlings'; the qRT-PCR time course runs 0 h to 14 d of N treatment, so 14 d may be the treatment duration rather than plant age. Recorded age_days = 14, phase steady.
proposed_answer: Keep phase steady (long-term HN vs LN); leave age_days 14 with this caveat.
evidence: Methods: 'Total RNAs were extracted from 14-day-old seedlings'; qRT-PCR at 0 h-14 d of nitrogen treatment; BioSample age 14day

question: Catalogue/accessions notes say PE150, but SRA runs have 150 bases per spot over 2 reads (2x75). Spot counts x2 match paper Table 1 raw reads exactly, so mapping is certain; only the read-length note is off.
proposed_answer: Record as PE 2x75; correct the catalogue note at the next catalogue pass.
evidence: runs.tsv n_bases/n_spots = 150, layout PAIRED; Table 1 raw reads = 2 x n_spots for all 12 libraries

question: All 18 runs share BioSample SAMN08706564 with generic titles; conditions and replicates come only from the ENA run aliases (submitted file names, e.g. RNA-Seq_-N_Replicate1_b.gz; libraries ZM1-ZM17). The trailing _a/_b is unexplained. Accept this mapping?
proposed_answer: Yes: Ctrl R1-R3 = SRR6829710/11/12, -N R1-R3 = SRR6829713/14/24, -P R1-R3 = SRR6829725/22/23. _a/_b treated as file-name suffixes (one run per library).
evidence: ENA filereport for SRP135301 (fields library_name, run_alias); runs.tsv biosample column.

question: -P samples have control N (5 mM NO3-) and low P; they are not part of any N contrast. Keep them?
proposed_answer: Keep include = TRUE (other_factor P supply = low P) so contrasts can ignore them; use only Ctrl vs -N for N.
evidence: PMC5917015 Methods (deficiency treatments) and spec rule for non-N samples.

question: Meng2020 only says 'WT'. Yu et al. 2016 (Sci Rep, PMC5137073) says the RNAi lines were made in Hi-II and introgressed into B73 as recurrent parent, with wild-type segregants as controls; R101 is ChromDB stock 3201-35. Curated WT as genotype_class B73 and RNAi background B73. Number of backcrosses not given.
proposed_answer: Keep B73 background; consider genotype_class 'other inbred' for WT if residual Hi-II introgression matters.
evidence: PMC5137073 Methods (Generation of transgenic plants); Meng2020 Methods cites Yu et al. 2016 for RS1 and R101

question: The 0 h samples are a time-zero baseline (BioSample nitrate '0 h'; paper 'nitrate treatment for 0 h' = mock), not a time-matched 2 h mock. The 2 h vs 0 h contrast includes 2 h of handling/diurnal change.
proposed_answer: Accept 2 h vs 0 h as the nitrate-resupply contrast within each genotype; note the caveat.
evidence: Methods: treated with 0.5 mM nitrate for 0 or 2 h; Fig. 4 legend: Mock, nitrate treatment for 0 h

question: Methods say seedlings were 'cultured in nitrate-free nutrient solution for 7 days', after 3 d germination and 4 d in water; figure legends say '7-day-old nitrate-free seedlings'. Age at sampling is therefore 7-14 d; age_days left empty.
proposed_answer: Leave empty.
evidence: Methods (Plant Material and Growth Conditions); Fig. 4 legend; BioSample dev_stage V1

question: Pre-growth used 'modified Hoagland's nutrient solution (Li et al., 2015) containing 0 mM nitrate'. Whether it held any other N source (e.g. ammonium) is not stated, and Li et al. 2015 (Plant Cell, not in PMC) was not checked. 0 h samples coded N_form none, N_amount 0.
proposed_answer: Keep 'none'/0 unless Li et al. 2015 shows an ammonium component.
evidence: Meng2020 Methods (Plant Material and Growth Conditions)

question: Each GSM has 3 runs under one SRX: one of about 17-18 M spots and two small ones (0.3-1.2 M). Are the small runs top-ups of the same library?
proposed_answer: Yes: same SRX/BioSample, so merged into one sample each (12 runs -> 4 samples).
evidence: runs.tsv experiment/biosample columns (SRX3434711-14).

question: Mu2017 says ’mature tissue of an expanding leaf’; GEO says ’the sixth Leaf’.
proposed_answer: tissue_detail ’leaf 6 maturation zone (50-150 mm from tip)’: Guo2022 (same lab, same experiment) reuses these libraries as its maturation-zone samples. other_factor ’leaf zone’ = maturation zone so Guo2022 contrasts can borrow them.
evidence: PMC5751227 Methods 4.4; PMC9230787 Methods 3.2 and data statement (GSE107562 + GSE111425).

question: Mu2017 figure legends say ’High nitrogen: 4 mM Ca(NO3)2; Low nitrogen: 40 uM Ca(NO3)2’ (8 mM and 80 uM NO3-), but Methods say 4.0 mM NO3- supplied as Ca(NO3)2.
proposed_answer: Use 4 and 0.04 mM nitrate (Methods, GEO ’4mM nitrogen’/’0.04mM nitrogen’, and Guo2022 all agree).
evidence: PMC5751227 Methods 4.1 vs Figure 2-3 legends; GEO characteristics.

question: The sampling date or age isn’t given (LN from leaf-3 full expansion, about 6 d after HN started; leaf 6 sampled while expanding).
proposed_answer: Leave age_days empty; stage as written.
evidence: PMC5751227 Methods 4.1-4.4; PMC9230787 Methods 3.1-3.2.

question: The 6 runs have only 0.95-10.6 M spots (SN_rep3 SRR10954073: 0.95 M; SN_rep2: 1.59 M; DN_rep3: 1.62 M) with variable average read lengths (83-148 nt), while the paper reports ~47 M PE reads per sample. Are the deposited files subsampled or pre-trimmed, and are they usable?
proposed_answer: Keep include = TRUE but flag low depth; check mapping rates and library size after quantification and consider dropping SN_rep3 if it fails QC.
evidence: runs.tsv n_spots/read_length for SRR10954070-75; PMC9806651 Results (RNA-seq section: about 47 million paired-end reads per sample) and Methods (reads trimmed to 100 nt).

question: SN fertilizer was ammonium sulfate (coded N_form = ammonium); DN received 0 kg N/ha supplemental N on an N-deficient soil (0.76 g/kg mineral N), coded none/0. OK?
proposed_answer: Yes: N_form ammonium (ammonium sulfate) for SN, none for DN, 240 vs 0 kg N/ha.
evidence: PMC9806651 Methods, Plant material and culture.

question: Field year is not reported, and the BioSamples give geo_loc_name American Samoa.
proposed_answer: Use the paper (Luhe Experimental Station, Nanjing, China); year NR.
evidence: PMC9806651 Methods; runs.tsv biosample_attributes geo_loc_name.

question: Every sample's GEO title and processed-file name (e.g. Cob_LN_rep1, GSM1440504_Cob_LN_rep1_TagCopyNumber) disagree with its GEO/BioSample treatment characteristic (Cob_LN_rep1-3 say 'optimal nitrogen supply', Cob_ON_rep1-3 say 'low nitrogen supply'; same for florets). N labels here follow title + file name. Accept, or swap?
proposed_answer: Follow titles (two submitter fields and the processed files agree; the characteristic looks like a template fill error). Verify after quantification: LN-vs-ON log2FC from these labels should match the direction of the paper's LN-responsive genes (Supplementary Tables S5/S8, mean TPM per group); swap all labels if they are reversed.
evidence: GEO GSE59613 GSM1440504-15 titles, supplementary file names and characteristics; runs.tsv biosample_attributes (same conflict)

question: These are 21-nt NlaIII DGE 3' tags (CATG + 17 nt), 49-nt reads (rep1-2) or 35-nt reads (rep3), mapped by the authors to maize v2. Curated now; processing deferred. Keep in v1 catalogue with processing deferred?
proposed_answer: Keep curated, defer processing; if processed, use a tag-aware pipeline (trim to 17-21 nt, unique-tag mapping to v5 transcripts + 300 nt UTR extension).
evidence: Paper Methods (PMC4588875); GEO data processing; runs.tsv read_length

question: Replicate 3 of every group was sequenced with 35-nt reads vs 49 nt for replicates 1-2 (a separate run). Batch is balanced across tissue x N, so include replicate/batch as a blocking factor?
proposed_answer: Yes: add batch (rep3 vs rep1-2) as a blocking term, or at least check it in PCA.
evidence: runs.tsv read_length 35 for SRR1521468, SRR1521471, SRR1521474, SRR1521477

question: ON = 250 kg N/ha split 60 (pre-sowing) + 120 (V8) + 70 (V12); fertilizer form and field year are not stated. N_form NR for ON. Accept?
proposed_answer: Accept NR (Chinese field trials usually use urea, but not stated).
evidence: Supplementary Table S1 (PDF); paper Methods; GEO growth protocol

question: The paper says root apices were pooled from 20 seedlings per replicate; GEO says each replicate had 10-15 plants.
proposed_answer: pooled_plants 20 (paper Methods).
evidence: PMC7013554 Methods 4.1-4.2; GEO GSE141860 overall design.

question: SRA lists Illumina HiSeq 2500; the paper says NextSeq500.
proposed_answer: Keep SRA metadata; no effect on the design (all 9 runs on one platform, so no within-study batch).
evidence: runs.tsv instrument; PMC7013554 Methods 4.2.

question: The -N and +NO3- samples are also Ravazzolo2021b’s controls; GSE173102 re-uploaded them (SRR14300957-62, identical read counts).
proposed_answer: Curate here only; Ravazzolo2021b contrasts borrow Ravazzolo2020_minusN_R1-3 and Ravazzolo2020_NO3_R1-3; never count them twice when pooling.
evidence: accessions_resolved.tsv; GSE173102 sample descriptions point to GSM4214790-95.

question: The study brief says each N level was run with and without TIS108 or PCIB, but GEO has only 4 groups: -N, +NO3-, -N + TIS108 and +NO3- + PCIB.
proposed_answer: Include all 12 samples. The N contrast is +NO3- vs -N (no inhibitor). TIS108 is usable only at -N and PCIB only at +NO3- (inhibitor contrasts); +NO3-+PCIB vs -N+TIS108 is not a valid N contrast.
evidence: GEO GSE162411 sample titles/characteristics; treatment protocol ’1 mM NO3-, 2 uM TIS108 and 1 mM NO3- plus 10 uM PCIB’.

question: GEO says ’primary root’ (whole primary root); the catalogue, from the accepted manuscript, says ’whole roots (4 seedlings pooled per replicate)’.
proposed_answer: tissue_detail ’primary root’ per GEO; check the accepted manuscript.
evidence: GEO source_name ’primary root’; catalogue tissue field.

question: GEO says 4-8 plants per replicate; the catalogue says 4 seedlings.
proposed_answer: Leave pooled_plants empty (a range isn’t a single number); note the 4-8 range.
evidence: GEO overall design; catalogue.

question: The catalogue says one +NO3- + PCIB replicate was left out of the paper’s DE analysis. GEO doesn’t say which one.
proposed_answer: Keep all 3 included for now; check the manuscript or post-alignment QC, and set include FALSE for the outlier if it’s identified.
evidence: catalogue bio_reps field (’1 replicate of +NO3- +PCIB excluded from DE’).

question: GEO says only that 3-d-old seedlings were treated for 24 h; the catalogue (manuscript) adds a 24 h N-deprivation before treatment.
proposed_answer: Follow the catalogue: age_days 5, phase resupply, time_h 24. GEO uses the same shorthand for Ravazzolo2020, whose paper confirms the pre-treatment.
evidence: GEO overall design; catalogue timepoints field; PMC7013554 Methods 4.1 for the sister study.

question: The nitrate counter-ion isn’t given (GEO says ’1 mM NO3-’).
proposed_answer: N_form nitrate, 1 mM; salt not stated (KNO3 in the lab’s sister studies).
evidence: GEO treatment protocol.

question: Only the 3 cPTIO libraries are new; the -N and +NO3- controls are Ravazzolo2020’s.
proposed_answer: Contrasts for this study borrow Ravazzolo2020_minusN_R1-3 and Ravazzolo2020_NO3_R1-3 (other_factor_level for them = no inhibitor). Its own valid N contrast is +NO3- vs -N, which belongs to Ravazzolo2020 (don’t duplicate it); cPTIO samples serve the +NO3-+cPTIO vs +NO3- inhibitor contrast.
evidence: PMC8431222 Methods 4.2 (’Datasets corresponding to -N and +NO3- treatments were already analyzed ... in a previous work’); accessions_resolved.tsv.

question: The paper kept only two of the three +NO3- + cPTIO replicates after QC; GEO deposits all three and doesn’t say which was dropped.
proposed_answer: Keep all 3 included for now; identify the outlier from Table S6 (in the paper’s supplementary zip) or our own QC, then set include FALSE for it.
evidence: PMC8431222 Methods 4.3 (’only two biological replicates were kept for the +NO3- + cPTIO treatment’).

question: The cPTIO libraries were deposited 16 months after the controls (GEO Apr 2021 vs Dec 2019) and GSE173102 lists ’TruSeq Stranded’ while GSE141860 lists ’TruSeq RNA’. The paper presents one experiment but doesn’t give sequencing dates.
proposed_answer: Treat as possible batch confounding between cPTIO and the borrowed controls; flag on any cPTIO contrast.
evidence: GEO GSE141860/GSE173102 submission dates and extract protocols; PMC8431222 Methods 4.1-4.2.

question: The paper says 20 pooled seedlings per replicate; GEO says 10-15 plants.
proposed_answer: pooled_plants 20 (paper).
evidence: PMC8431222 Methods 4.2; GEO GSE173102 overall design.

item: duplicate reads across the two runs per library
question: Each library has two SRA runs, but they are not two lanes: HS_<lib> runs are BAMs aligned to H. seropedicae (with unmapped reads, i.e. the full read set) and AGPv4_<lib> runs are TopHat BAMs of the maize-aligned subset of the same reads. Merging them would double-count maize reads. How to handle?
proposed_answer: Quantify each library from its HS_ run only (SRR27000651/652/657/658/660/663/664, SRR27110053); set the AGPv4_ runs (SRR27000653/654/655/656/659/661/662, SRR27110054) to include=FALSE in runs.tsv, or skip them in the pipeline. Both are listed in run_accessions here because the spec requires every included run once.
evidence: ENA filereport (library_name, submitted file names, e.g. HseropedicaeZ67_190521_SND405_B_L003_FAS-2341.pe.bam vs AGPv4_190521_SND405_B_L003_FAS-2341.pe.bam); HS_ runs: 27.5-33.7 M pairs, fixed 2x125 nt, sum 247.8 M pairs = 495.7 M reads, matching the paper's '495 million paired-end reads'; AGPv4_ runs: 1.8-21.7 M pairs, variable length.

question: Paper text and Table 1 say '0.3 / 3 mM of nitrate', but Supplementary Table S1 gives N as both NO3- and NH4+. Which form to record?
proposed_answer: mixed: 0.3 mM N = 0.25 mM NO3- + 0.05 mM NH4+; 3 mM N = 2.5 mM NO3- + 0.5 mM NH4+ (5:1). Recorded N_form=mixed, N_amount = total N.
evidence: PMC10965572 Supplementary Table S1 (N-NO3- 3.5/35 mg/L, N-NH4+ 0.7/7 mg/L for the 0.3/3.0 mM solutions); Methods 2.1 cites Table S1 for the hydroponic solution.

question: SHS 5050 is called both an 'inbred line' and 'a triple hybrid' in the paper. Which class?
proposed_answer: hybrid (Santa Helena SHS 5050 is a commercial triple-cross hybrid).
evidence: PMC10965572 Methods 2.1: 'the maize inbred line Santa Helena SHS 5050, which is a triple hybrid'; BioSample cultivar 'Santa Helena SHS 5050'.

question: Only 2 replicates per condition were sequenced, and replicate is confounded with sequencing batch (FAS libraries on the 2019-05-21 run, ADSF libraries on the 2019-06-05 run). Batch is balanced (one replicate of each condition per batch). Use batch as a blocking factor?
proposed_answer: Yes: model ~ batch + condition (replicate 1 = FAS batch, replicate 2 = ADSF batch).
evidence: ENA submitted file names (190521 ... B_L003 vs 190605 ... A_L007); paper Methods 2.1: five replicates grown, two sent for sequencing.

question: BioSample says age 24 days; paper implies 4 d germination + 18 DAI = 22 d. Which age?
proposed_answer: 22 d (paper); minor.
evidence: PMC10965572 Methods 2.1 and Fig. 1A legend; BioSample SAMN38518077 age=24 days.

question: Each genotype x tissue x N group has a single library (8 runs total). How should SE be obtained for pooling?
proposed_answer: Keep include=TRUE; contrasts need a variance strategy (e.g. a shared dispersion across the 4 genotype x tissue groups or a down-weighting rule), or exclude from SE-weighted pooling.
evidence: PMC8913646 Methods ('eight cDNA libraries were constructed'); BioSample aliquote 'replicate 1' for all.

question: The working N concentration of the N-sufficient Hoagland is not reported (only 1 M stocks of KNO3, Ca(NO3)2, NH4H2PO4). Record NR?
proposed_answer: NR (rank 2). Standard Hoagland No. 2 would be about 15 mM N (14 NO3- + 1 NH4+), but the paper does not say.
evidence: PMC8913646 Methods (plant material, stress treatment).

item: platform/batch by tissue and P level
question: Leaf libraries were sequenced on HiSeq 4000 (UC Berkeley) and root libraries on NextSeq 550 (Labsergen); within leaves, lane batch DRRS001 holds every full-P library and DRRS002 every low-P library. N contrasts are within tissue and within P level, so they are not confounded; P main effects in leaf are confounded with lane batch. OK to use N contrasts within each tissue x P level?
proposed_answer: Yes: build N contrasts (LowN vs Full, LowNP vs LowP) within tissue and P level only; record the batch caveat for any P or tissue comparison.
evidence: BioSample sample_fastq DRRS001_* = fullN_fullP/lowN_fullP, DRRS002_* = fullN_lowP/lowN_lowP; instrument column in runs.tsv; Methods (RNA-seq section)

question: Only 2 biological replicates (single plants) per tissue x treatment. Keep the study for pooling?
proposed_answer: Keep; SEs will be large and the meta-analysis weights will reflect that.
evidence: Methods: 2 tissues x 4 treatments x 2 replicates = 16 samples; Results: two individuals per treatment

question: The 16 wild-type runs are curated here only; AlonsoNieves2022 reuses them as its WT reference. Contrast building for AlonsoNieves2022 genotype effects must pull these samples from this study without double-counting N effects in pooling.
proposed_answer: Count WT N contrasts once (under TorresRodriguez2021); AlonsoNieves2022 contributes only het/hom N contrasts.
evidence: runs.tsv also_used_by = AlonsoNieves2022; AlonsoNieves2022 Methods: separate analysis of WT libraries published previously

question: CK = sole NO3- (100/0), T1 = 75%/25% NO3-/NH4+, T2 = sole NH4+ (0/100), all at 1 mM total N; ranks tie (1). One Methods sentence words the preliminary optimum as an NH4+ to NO3- ratio of 75%/25%, but the abstract, figure legends and BioSamples all say 75% nitrate. Accept?
proposed_answer: Accept; form contrasts T1 vs CK (mixed vs nitrate) and T2 vs CK (ammonium vs nitrate) within tissue.
evidence: Abstract; Fig. 4 legend (SCK/ST1/ST2 = sole NO3-, mixed N, sole NH4+); BioSample isolate (100/0, 75/25, 0/100 nitrate and ammonium ratio)

question: Sampling time for RNA-seq is not stated explicitly; biomass was sampled 12 d after transplanting and BioSamples say 12d Hydroponics. Stage recorded as 12 d after transplanting; age_days empty.
proposed_answer: Accept 12 d of treatment.
evidence: Methods (Biomass...); BioSample dev_stage 12d Hydroponics

question: A1-3 = untreated (-N, before nitrate supply) and B1-3 = treated (+N, 30 min after nitrate). Supported by alias (root_-N_x / root_+N_x), BioSample tissue (root_before_treatment / root_after_treatment) and paper Table S1 fragment counts. But the BioSample treatment attribute of B1-3 says Before N supply. Accept the alias/tissue/Table S1 reading?
proposed_answer: Accept: A = untreated, B = treated; the B treatment attribute is a copy-paste error (PacBio Long_+N says After N supply).
evidence: runs.tsv aliases and tissue attributes; Table S1 (MOESM7): Untreated_1-3 17.5/21.5/18.5 M, Treated_1-3 22.0/20.5/18.0 M vs spots A1-3 17.53/21.51/18.96 M, B1-3 22.25/20.70/18.42 M

question: The nitrate concentration supplied for the 30 min treatment is not stated (SN solution in this paper is 15 mM KNO3). N_amount = NR for treated samples; rank 2 vs untreated (0.15 mM) is safe.
proposed_answer: Keep NR (likely 15 mM KNO3, as in SN and in Ge2020, but not stated).
evidence: Methods (Plant materials and growth conditions); Results (RNA-seq identifies early-response genes)

question: Untreated DN-grown roots coded phase steady, 0.15 mM nitrate, time_h 0 (same convention as Du2020/Wu2024 time-0 baselines); treated coded resupply, time_h 0.5. There is no time-matched mock.
proposed_answer: Keep; contrast = 30 min vs 0 min.
evidence: Results: untreated sample vs treated with nitrate at 30 min

item: germination N status and phase coding
question: Seeds germinated 48 h on 'moistened filter paper' (medium not stated) before transfer to CK (2 mM N) or LN (0). Coded as N-free germination: S0 = none/0 (rank 1, time_h 0), CK = resupply (N first supplied at time 0), LN = steady (still N-free). OK?
proposed_answer: Yes (standard water germination; nutrient solution only mentioned after transfer). Main contrasts: LN vs CK time-matched at S1/S2/S3 (24/48/72 h). If germination medium contained N, CK and LN would become steady and starvation instead, and S0 N would be NR.
evidence: PMC9498817 Methods 2.1 (seeds soaked in saturated CaSO4, germinated between moistened filter paper, then rolls placed in nutrient solution) and 2.4 (RNA-seq: germinated 48 h = S0, then transferred to CK/LN).

question: S0 BioSamples say tissue=root, but the paper only says 'ten germinated seedlings were collected' (S1-S3 are explicitly primary roots). Root or whole seedling?
proposed_answer: Root per BioSample (tissue_group Root, no PO term); could be whole germinated seedling. Low impact: S0 is only a time-zero reference.
evidence: PMC9498817 Methods 2.4; BioSample tissue=root for all 21 samples (blanket value).

question: The RNA-seq text implies transfer to CK/LN right after 48 h germination, while the GWAS protocol transferred 3-d-old seedlings after a period in full nutrient solution. Age at S1-S3 left empty. OK?
proposed_answer: Leave age_days empty for S1-S3 (likely 3-5 d); time_h records 24/48/72 h since transfer.
evidence: PMC9498817 Methods 2.1 vs 2.4.

question: BioSample ecotype is B73 for all 12 samples, but the paper made Zmnrt2.5-1 in ND101 and uses ND101 as wild type. Which is right?
proposed_answer: ND101 (paper). Can be checked from reads: ND101 vs B73 SNPs, and the 1-bp deletion near the start of ZmNRT2.5 (Zm00001d011679) in the cas9 samples only.
evidence: PMC11933875: 'generated a mutant of ZmNRT2.5 using CRISPR/Cas9 ... in the inbred line ND101'; RNA-seq of 'wild-type (ND101) plants and the Zmnrt2.5-1 mutant'. runs.tsv biosample_attributes ecotype=B73.

question: BioSample says husk leaf; paper says RNA-seq 'of ears (about 5.0 cm in length)' / 'ear tissue' to study husk-leaf expression; catalogue says Ear/kernel. Which tissue_group?
